passages.text: See the information under the caption “Management’s Discussion and Analysis.” ITEM 7A. QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK. We are exposed to a variety of market risks, including interest rates and currency exchange rates. We attempt to actively manage these risks. See the information under “Management’s Discussion and Analysis,” under “Financial Instrument Market Risk Information” and in Note 26 to the Consolidated Financial Statements. ITEM 8. FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND SUPPLEMENTARY DATA. See the Consolidated Financial Statements and notes thereto and supplementary data. ITEM 9. CHANGES IN AND DISAGREEMENTS WITH ACCOUNTANTS ON ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE. Not applicable. ITEM 9A. CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES. Disclosure Controls and Procedures Our principal executive officer and our principal financial officer have concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the Exchange Act)) were effective as of November 2, 2025, based on the evaluation of these controls and procedures required by Rule 13a-15(b) or 15d-15(b) of the Exchange Act. Management’s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting Management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting. Our internal control system was designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the preparation and fair presentation of published financial statements in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles. All internal control systems, no matter how well designed, have inherent limitations. Therefore, even those systems determined to be effective can provide only reasonable assurance with respect to financial statement preparation and presentation in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. Management assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of November 2, 2025, using the criteria set forth in Internal Control – Integrated Framework (2013) issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. Based on that assessment, management concluded that, as of November 2, 2025, our internal control over financial reporting was effective. Our independent registered public accounting firm has issued an audit report on the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting. That report is included herein. Changes in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting During the fourth quarter of 2025, there were no changes that have materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect our internal control over financial reporting. This Annual Report on Form 10-K contains forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. All statements other than statements of historical fact included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K are forward-looking statements. Forward-looking statements provide our current expectations and projections relating to our financial condition, results of operations, plans, objectives, future performance, and business. You can identify forward-looking statements as they do not relate to historical or current facts and by words such as “believe,” “expect,” “estimate,” “anticipate,” “will,” “aim,” “should,” “plan,” “forecast,” “target,” “guide,” “project,” “intend,” “could,” and similar words or expressions. All forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ materially from those that we expected. Important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from our expectations, or cautionary statements, and other important information about forward-looking statements are disclosed under Item 1A, “Risk Factors,” and Item 7, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations–Forward-Looking Statements,” in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. As used herein, the terms “John Deere,” “we,” “us,” “our,” or “the Company” refer collectively to Deere & Company and its subsidiaries, unless designated or identified otherwise. All amounts are presented in millions of U.S. dollars, unless otherwise specified. Products John Deere has manufactured agricultural equipment since 1837. Deere & Company was incorporated under the laws of Delaware in 1958. Our business is managed through the following four business segments: Production & Precision Agriculture (PPA), Small Agriculture & Turf (SAT), Construction & Forestry (CF), and Financial Services (John Deere Financial or FS).

credit_strengths.text: Deere's balance sheet carries net cash, with unrestricted cash exceeding interest-bearing debt, so gross leverage sits far below the Industrials sector median and the indicative financial risk profile is Minimal. This cushion absorbs cyclical downturns in farm equipment demand without pressuring the capital structure.

Operating cash flow comfortably funds capital expenditure, leaving substantial free cash flow that covers reported debt by a wide margin. Cash generation is diversified across Production & Precision Agriculture, Small Agriculture & Turf, Construction & Forestry and Financial Services, supporting through-cycle debt service.

key_risks.text: Revenue has declined for two consecutive fiscal years, reflecting weaker global agricultural equipment demand. The risk-factor passage highlights forward-looking uncertainty around farm income, input costs and trade conditions. Analyst judgement: earnings could compress further if the downcycle extends, though operating margin remains above the sector median.

Reported debt is a partial sum of itemized instrument tags, excluding leases and possibly untagged facilities, so true leverage may be understated. The debt note shows near-term maturities exceeding cash on hand, requiring refinancing or cash flow. Analyst judgement: refinancing risk is manageable given net cash, but disclosure gaps warrant monitoring.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is below the sector median, indicating less headroom than peers, yet absolute operating income covers interest expense multiple times. Free cash flow to debt is strong, and net cash means debt service is not reliant on refinancing. Analyst judgement: coverage should remain adequate unless earnings deteriorate sharply.

Operating cash flow declined year over year but still funds capital expenditure and shareholder returns. Dividends and buybacks absorb a large share of free cash flow, leaving limited buffer if cash generation weakens. Analyst judgement: distributions are sustainable at current earnings but could pressure liquidity in a prolonged downturn.

overall_credit_view.text: Deere's net cash position, Minimal indicative financial risk profile and strong free cash flow support a high investment-grade credit view. Leverage is well below the sector median and interest coverage, while lower than peers, remains adequate. Analyst judgement: the credit profile is resilient, with capacity to absorb cyclical weakness.

The main credit considerations are the revenue downcycle, partial debt disclosure and shareholder distributions that consume most free cash flow. Missing current assets and liabilities limit liquidity analysis, but net cash mitigates near-term refinancing risk. Analyst judgement: stable outlook, contingent on farm equipment demand stabilising.

credit_strengths.text: Deere 的資產負債表持有淨現金，未受限現金超過計息債務，因此總槓桿遠低於工業行業中位數，指示性財務風險狀況為極低。此緩衝可吸收農機設備需求的週期性下滑，而不會對資本結構造成壓力。
營運現金流足以輕鬆支應資本支出，留下可觀的自由現金流，並以較大差距覆蓋呈報債務。現金產生分散於生產與精準農業、小型農業與草坪、建築與林業以及金融服務，支持全週期債務償付。

key_risks.text: 收入已連續兩個財政年度下降，反映全球農業設備需求轉弱。風險因素段落強調圍繞農場收入、投入成本及貿易狀況的前瞻性不確定性。分析師判斷：若下行週期延長，盈利可能進一步壓縮，儘管營業利潤率仍高於行業中位數。
呈報債務是逐項工具標籤的部分總和，不包括租賃及可能未標記的融資安排，因此真實槓桿可能被低估。債務附註顯示短期到期債務超過手頭現金，需要再融資或現金流。分析師判斷：鑑於淨現金，再融資風險可控，但披露缺口值得監察。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率低於行業中位數，表明緩衝空間少於同業，但絕對營業利潤仍以倍數覆蓋利息支出。自由現金流對債務比率強勁，且淨現金意味著債務償付不依賴再融資。分析師判斷：除非盈利急劇惡化，覆蓋率應保持充足。
營運現金流同比下降，但仍足以支應資本支出及股東回報。股息及回購吸收自由現金流的很大份額，若現金產生轉弱，留下的緩衝有限。分析師判斷：按當前盈利水平，分派可持續，但在長期低迷中可能對流動性造成壓力。

overall_credit_view.text: Deere 的淨現金狀況、極低的指示性財務風險狀況及強勁的自由現金流支持較高的投資級信用觀點。槓桿遠低於行業中位數，而利息覆蓋率雖低於同業，仍屬充足。分析師判斷：信用狀況具韌性，有能力吸收週期性疲弱。
主要信用考量是收入下行週期、部分債務披露以及消耗大部分自由現金流的股東分派。缺少流動資產及流動負債限制了流動性分析，但淨現金緩解短期再融資風險。分析師判斷：展望穩定，取決於農機設備需求趨穩。
